ground_truth_soap:
Subjective:

   Chief Complaint (CC):
   - Multiple cravings per day and mood swings when unable to smoke.

   History of Present Illness (HPI):
   - The patient is a 38-year-old Hispanic female presenting for the initial consultation regarding smoking cessation. She has a 25-year history of smoking, currently consuming 20 cigarettes daily. She reports associated symptoms of persistent cough and morning phlegm production. She experiences interruptions at work due to frequent smoking breaks, which leads to decreased productivity. She has had previous failed attempts to quit smoking.

   Review of Systems (ROS):
   - General: Reports difficulty staying asleep, approximately 4-5 hours of sleep per night.
   - Respiratory: Persistent cough, morning phlegm.
   - Psychiatric: Mood swings, especially when unable to smoke.
   - Social: High alcohol consumption on weekends (10-15 drinks), occasional marijuana use, leads a sedentary lifestyle, consumes mostly processed and high-fat foods.

Objective:

   Vital Signs:
   - Height: 165 cm
   - Weight: 90 kg
   - BMI: 33.1 (indicative of obesity)
   - Blood pressure: 138/88 mmHg
   - Heart rate: 88 bpm

   Physical Examination:
   - General: Appears in no acute distress but looks fatigued.
   - Respiratory: Chest auscultation reveals wheezing and rhonchi.
   - Cardiovascular: No murmurs, regular rhythm.
   - Abdomen: Non-tender, no hepatosplenomegaly.
   - Extremities: No edema, peripheral pulses intact.

Assessment:

   - Nicotine dependence, cigarettes, uncomplicated (ICD-10: F17.210).
   - Contributing factors include chronic bronchitis and obesity.
   - Social factors: low income, limited access to healthcare facilities and healthy food options, high alcohol usage, occasional marijuana use.

Plan:

   Medications:
   - Prescribed Bupropion SR, 150 mg, oral, once daily for 3 days, then increase to twice daily. Dispense 60 tablets.

   Behavioral Therapy:
   - Referred to Dr. Emily Rodriguez, Psychologist, for a smoking cessation program.

   Lifestyle Changes:
   - Advised to incorporate more vegetables and fruits into her diet.
   - Recommended moderate exercise like walking 30 minutes daily.

   Follow-Up:
   - Scheduled a follow-up appointment in 6 weeks to monitor progress and potential side effects.

   Additional Recommendations:
   - Discussed reducing alcohol consumption to lower overall health risks.
   - Encouraged developing better sleep hygiene practices to improve sleep duration and quality.
   - Provided educational materials in Spanish to improve health literacy.

   Instructions:
   - The patient will need to return for a follow-up to discuss the results of the pulmonary function test and blood tests.
   - Advised to contact the clinic if experiencing any side effects from the medication or if there are any questions or concerns regarding the treatment plan.

   Barriers:
   - Discussed potential difficulties in affording medications and accessing resources due to her low income; provided information about potential financial assistance programs and community resources.
